title: Skitter and the Shimmer-Slug's Secret Stairs
markdown:
Waterfalls tumbled down steep rocks like shiny ribbons. Old stairs, carved long ago, went up and up to the misty tops. In this land of ravens and echoes lived Skitter, a goblin with bright curious eyes, a nose that twitched with constant thought, and a heart as soft as the moss in his tiny cave-home. His best friend was Bracket, a crow sleek and sharp as a polished shadow.

Skitter’s greatest treasure was Pip, a shimmer-slug. Pip left a trail of faint pearly glow wherever he slithered, like spilled moonlight. He also loved to burrow into the most inconvenient places: a hollow acorn, a forgotten teapot.

“Pip, my little light. Are you comfortable in that teacup again? It’s not good for your slime.” Pip would usually wiggle, content.

This time Pip had truly outdone himself. Skitter had been polishing river-worn stones when he noticed the slug missing. A fluttery unwelcome feeling. He searched the cave, patted every nook. Nothing. The favourite mushroom patch outside, cheerful red caps. Nothing.

Then his sharp goblin eyes caught it: a tiny almost invisible crack in the rock face, barely wider than his thumb, leading into the mountain’s dark silent heart. From it, a faint shimmering trail of pearly light. Pip.

“Oh, Pip. The most inconvenient place. How will I ever get you out?”

Bracket landed on his shoulder with a soft caw. Intelligent eyes twinkling with concern. “Trouble, friend Skitter?”

“Pip’s gone inside the mountain. Into that crack. He’ll be lost in the dark.”

A melodic strum. On a high ledge, a shimmering elf with a harp, robes the colour of twilight. “Ah, Skitter, going on an adventure. Looking for your lost Pip, the luminous slug.”

Skitter blinked. “Adventure? I just want my pet back.”

The elf, Lirael, merely smiled. Skitter felt a little annoyed. “If you’re going to be mysterious, you could at least be helpful.” But Lirael was already weaving a melody that made Skitter feel a little like a hero from a story. He did not need a song about friendship. He needed a coil of vine.

He gathered dried berries, sturdy vine his nimble fingers had woven, and his most determined sigh. Bracket took off, a dark shape against the vast blue, scanning the path ahead. Skitter squeezed through the crack, which widened into a narrow twisting passage. Air cooler. Silence hummed with a deep earthy sound, like the mountain breathing.

They descended. Stairways carved into the rock went down and down. Skitter’s heart hammered. Bracket’s occasional caws were a promise of companionship.

They came to a bridge spanning a deep roaring gorge. Water churned like a hungry beast, frothing, crashing, mist tickling Skitter’s nose. Beneath the bridge, clinging to damp stone, thousands of glow-worms pulsed with soft emerald light, a starry carpet, a secret world within a secret world.

“Incredible,” Skitter whispered.

They pressed on. A grumpy rock troll, round and grey as a weathered boulder, blocked a crucial junction. “None shall pass without answering my riddle. What has a slimy trail, loves cozy holes, and makes a path of light?”

Skitter pictured Pip happily burrowing. “My pet shimmer-slug, Pip.”

The troll grunted like rocks tumbling. “Well played, little goblin. You may pass.”

Passages grew more complex, a labyrinth. A prickle of doubt. Where was Pip? Had he gone too far?

“Don’t give up,” Bracket cawed, nudging Skitter’s cheek. “He’s nearby. I feel it.”

Then the path ended at a sheer wall of smooth unforgiving rock. No cracks, no openings, not even a wisp of shimmer. Skitter sank down. The tiny pouch of berries tumbled onto the dusty floor. He felt small, not brave. The silence pressed in, heavy.

Then, just above his head: a faint pearly shimmer. Pip’s trail. Not going down. Going up the sheer wall.

“Up?” A flicker of hope. He looked at the luminous slime, at the sturdy vine. An idea, bright as Pip’s own shimmer.

He grabbed the vine and, using the slippery luminous trail as a guide, began to climb. The slime was surprisingly sticky, just enough grip. Bracket circled, caws full of encouragement. Higher. Goblin fingers finding purchase where none seemed to exist.

There, nestled in a small mossy crevice near the cave ceiling, Pip curled into a perfect shimmering ball, fast asleep, utterly unaware of the worry he had caused. Skitter scooped him up. Pip wriggled happily, a tiny contented sigh, a fresh trail of light on Skitter’s hand.

“You found the most inconvenient, yet perfect, spot.”

They climbed back down, Pip nestled in the satchel, soft breathing a calming sound. Lirael’s harp was a faint thread somewhere above, but Skitter did not wait for an announcement. They emerged into bright highland air. Bracket perched proudly. Skitter held Pip close and simply smiled. The dark had been long. The stair had been secret. The slug, inconvenient as ever, was warm against his palm, and already considering the teapot.
characters: Skitter (goblin with a soft heart), Bracket (a crow as sharp as polished shadow)
audience: children aged 9-10, amusing fantasy story for middle-grade readers
author: StoryGen Community
